decks.notes: This deck focuses on quickly establishing a board presence with aggressive creatures while disrupting the opponent's game plan with hate cards like Thalia, Guardian of Thraben and Chancellor of the Annex. It aims to slow down the opponent's spells with tax effects and denial lands like Wasteland and Strip Mine, while also utilizing powerful artifacts like Moxes and Solitude for removal and tempo advantage. The deck's strategy is to apply pressure while controlling the game, ultimately overwhelming the opponent with a mix of aggression and disruption.

This deck focuses on setting up a powerful combo using Coveted Jewel as the central piece. By ramping mana quickly with cards like Grim Monolith and Mishra's Workshop, the deck aims to generate enough resources to cast Paradoxical Outcome and draw into key pieces like Tinker or Time Vault. Using artifacts like Mox Opal and Mana Crypt, the deck can create explosive turns and utilize cards like Gitaxian Probe and Sensei's Divining Top to sculpt its hand and draw into the combo. Overall, the strategy revolves around quickly assembling a winning combination while controlling the game with counterspells and disruptive artifacts.

This deck focuses on using planeswalkers and powerful control spells to dominate the board and disrupt the opponent's strategy. By utilizing efficient removal spells, counterspells, and disruptive cards like Collector Ouphe, it can control the game and protect its own game plan. The key to success lies in managing resources effectively, using the planeswalkers' abilities to generate advantage, and setting up powerful card advantage engines like Sylvan Library and Expressive Iteration. Overall, the deck aims to outvalue the opponent and establish control of the game through its powerful spells and planeswalker abilities.

The deck focuses on generating tons of mana quickly using artifacts like Grim Monolith and Mox Opal, while also utilizing cards like Paradoxical Outcome to draw through the deck. The win condition revolves around assembling the Time Vault + Voltaic Key combo to take extra turns, with Coveted Jewel acting as a backup win condition. The deck also includes disruptive elements like Trinisphere, Force of Will, and Karn, the Great Creator to control the game and protect the combo. Mystic Forge and Urza's Saga provide additional card advantage and utility.

The main focus of this deck is to quickly fill the graveyard with cards such as Golgari Grave-Troll and Golgari Thug using cards like Bazaar of Baghdad and Serum Powder. By doing so, the player can then utilize the graveyard to bring back creatures like Ichorid and Prized Amalgam to overwhelm the opponent with a strong board presence. Additionally, the deck includes disruption elements like Force of Will and Chalice of the Void to protect the combo pieces and control the game tempo. Overall, the deck aims to efficiently and aggressively combo off to secure a victory.

This Vintage 1 vs 1 deck, known as Bazaar Aggro, focuses on aggressive gameplay. The key concept revolves around utilizing cards like Bazaar of Baghdad to quickly fill the graveyard and take advantage of cards that benefit from having cards in the graveyard, such as Vengevine and Hollow One. The deck also includes various disruptive elements like Chalice of the Void and Force of Will to hinder opponents' strategies. Additionally, the deck incorporates powerful recursion effects like Squee, Goblin Nabob and Noxious Revival to constantly bring back threats from the graveyard.

The main concept of this deck is to aggressively utilize the graveyard and powerful creatures to overwhelm the opponent quickly. The deck focuses on cards that can be played for free or at a reduced cost, such as Hogaak, Arisen Necropolis and Vengevine, to establish a strong board presence early in the game. With cards like Once Upon a Time and Bazaar of Baghdad for card selection and ramping, the deck aims to consistently put pressure on the opponent and disrupt their strategy with cards like Collector Ouphe and Force of Vigor.

The deck focuses on overwhelming the opponent with aggressive creatures while disrupting their game with hate cards. The key strategy is to deploy hatebears like Thalia, Guardian of Thraben and Archon of Emeria to slow down the opponent's plays and prevent them from casting spells efficiently. The aggro aspect of the deck is supported by efficient creatures like Solitude and White Plume Adventurer, backed up by powerful mana acceleration from Moxen and Ancient Tomb. The mana base is also designed to disrupt the opponent's lands with Wasteland and Strip Mine, further increasing the deck's disruptive capabilities.

The deck focuses on assembling the combo of Coveted Jewel and exploiting artifact mana sources to generate an overwhelming advantage. Using cards like Mishra's Workshop and Grim Monolith, the deck accelerates its mana production to play powerful spells like Tinker to tutor for Time Vault. The deck also features disruptive elements like Force of Will to protect its key cards and Urza's Saga to tutor for artifact lands. By combining card advantage, fast mana, and a powerful win condition, the deck aims to overwhelm its opponent quickly.

The deck focuses on playing aggressive creatures that also disrupt the opponent's strategy, known as Hatebears. By using cards like Thalia, Guardian of Thraben and Archon of Emeria, the deck slows down the opponent's spells while deploying threats of its own. The deck also includes removal spells like Solitude and disrupts mana bases with cards like Chancellor of the Annex and Wasteland. The goal is to apply pressure while disrupting the opponent's game plan, ultimately overwhelming them with a combination of aggression and disruption.

This deck revolves around assembling powerful artifacts like Grim Monolith, Tinker, and Coveted Jewel to generate massive amounts of mana and draw cards with Paradoxical Outcome. By using cards like Urza's Saga, Karn, the Great Creator, and Mystic Forge, the deck can search for key pieces or combo off quicker. The inclusion of disruptive cards like Force of Will and Trinisphere help protect the combo and slow down the opponent. The overall strategy is to race to assemble the combo pieces and overwhelm the opponent with mana and card advantage to win the game.

The key concept of this deck is to aggressively disrupt the opponent's game plan while applying pressure with hatebears and efficient creatures. By utilizing cards like Thalia, Guardian of Thraben and Archon of Emeria to tax the opponent and slow them down, combined with cards like Solitude and Anointed Peacekeeper to control the board, this aggro-hatebear deck aims to overwhelm the opponent and secure victory through a combination of disruption and aggression. The deck also includes powerful mana acceleration in the form of Moxen and fast lands like Ancient Tomb to help establish an early advantage.

The main concept of this Vintage 1 vs 1 control deck is to utilize Painter's Servant and Grindstone as a win condition. By using Goblin Engineer and Enlightened Tutor to search for the necessary pieces, the deck aims to assemble the combo and mill the opponent's library in order to win the game. Additional cards like Voltaic Key, Manifold Key, and Lurrus of the Dream-Den provide support and utility, while other mana acceleration cards like Mox Jet, Mox Pearl, and Mana Crypt help to generate the necessary resources for executing the combo efficiently.

The main strategy of this Vintage 1 vs 1 Control deck is to disrupt the opponent's game plan by utilizing powerful artifacts and disruptive permanents like Smokestack, Sphere of Resistance, and Trinisphere. It aims to control the board through stax effects and mana denial, while also generating card advantage with cards like Crucible of Worlds and Karn, the Great Creator. The deck emphasizes resource denial and lockout effects, eventually overwhelming the opponent with a combination of mana denial, card advantage, and disruptive threats.

The main focus of this deck is to generate massive amounts of mana through cards like Grim Monolith and Mox Opal, allowing for explosive plays with cards like Tinker and Paradoxical Outcome. The key combo piece in this deck is Coveted Jewel, which can generate even more mana and card advantage. The inclusion of cards like Karn, the Great Creator and Mystic Forge allows for additional utility and card selection. Overall, this deck aims to quickly assemble its combo pieces and overwhelm the opponent with its powerful synergies.

This deck revolves around controlling the game by using cards like Force of Will, Flusterstorm, and Mental Misstep to counter your opponent's spells. It also utilizes Oath of Druids to bring powerful creatures into play quickly. The deck includes ways to search for specific cards like Demonic Tutor and Vampiric Tutor, as well as powerful removal spells like Assassin's Trophy and Pernicious Deed. Additionally, it includes powerful planeswalkers like Oko, Thief of Crowns, and protection cards like Veil of Summer to help maintain board control and ensure victory.
